newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends lower amid some hedge selling.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends lower amid some hedge selling.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended lower, surrendering early gains to some hedge pressure, traders said.

"We again reflected Chicago (CBOT) soybeans but we did not go as low as they did nor as high as they did. We did not have the big swings, we were more moderate," a canola trader said of futures trade at the two exchanges so far this week.
CBOT soybeans ended three to 5-3/4 cents higher.
Toward the end of the canola session, local short covering and light commercial buying lifted prices off their session lows, he added.

Flax was well underpinned by commercial buying, the trader said. But he noted "no commercial was willing to chase the flax market." January canola was off $0.50 at $402.50 a tonne and January flax eased $0.20 at $349.80.
February western barley gained $0.70 at $136.40 and March feed wheat gained $1.20 to $170.00. March oats rose $US1.00 at $US115.00 and February feed peas stood unchanged at US$206.00.
Barley ended firmer amid continued commission house short covering in May and July which lent support to other months. Commercials were also buyers, a second trader said.
Oats and peas did not trade.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
